drivingQuestion: How do the Rabbis answer Rabbi Eliezer's claim that a farmer's oxen and a driver's donkey are tools of his craft?
outcomeNote: The dispute is located in whether working animals count as tools of a craft.

segments.he: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיָה אִיכָּר, נוֹתֵן לוֹ צִמְדּוֹ. וְרַבָּנַן? הָנְהוּ לָאו כְּלֵי אוּמָּנוּת נִינְהוּ, אֶלָּא נְכָסִים נִינְהוּ.
segments.en: The mishna teaches: «Rabbi Eliezer says» that «if he was a farmer,» the treasurer «gives him his pair» of oxen; if he was a donkey driver, the treasurer gives him his donkey. The Gemara asks: «And the Rabbis,» why do they rule that these animals are repossessed? The Gemara responds: According to the Rabbis, «these» animals «are not tools of» his «craft; rather, they are» his «property.»
